{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{cgroup_8c_af4ef2481171a0a19ee0f4d5e12ea3616} 
enum \doxymbox{\hyperlink{cgroup_8c_af4ef2481171a0a19ee0f4d5e12ea3616}{cgroup2\+\_\+param}}}

Enumeration Description:\+ This enumeration defines the mount options available for cgroup2 (the default hierarchy). Each value represents a specific mount parameter that can be passed during cgroup2 mount operations. Options include Opt\+\_\+nsdelegate (use namespaces as delegation boundaries), Opt\+\_\+favordynmods (enable per-\/threadgroup locking for better performance), Opt\+\_\+memory\+\_\+localevents (enable legacy local memory events), Opt\+\_\+memory\+\_\+recursiveprot (enable recursive subtree protection), Opt\+\_\+memory\+\_\+hugetlb\+\_\+accounting (enable hugetlb accounting for the memory controller), and Opt\+\_\+pids\+\_\+localevents (enable legacy local pids events). The nr\+\_\+\+\_\+cgroup2\+\_\+params value at the end indicates the total count of options. \begin{DoxyEnumFields}[2]{Enumerator}

cgroup\+\_\+add\+\_\+cftypes -\/ add an array of cftypes to a subsystem @ss:\+ target cgroup subsystem @cfts:\+ zero-\/length name terminated array of cftypes

Register @cfts to @ss. Files described by @cfts are created for all existing cgroups to which @ss is attached and all future cgroups will have them too. This function can be called anytime whether @ss is attached or not.

Returns 0 on successful registration, -\/errno on failure. Note that this function currently returns 0 as long as @cfts registration is successful even if some file creation attempts on existing cgroups fail.

Function Description:\+ Adds an array of cftypes to a subsystem. It creates files for all existing cgroups. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

cgroup\+\_\+apply\+\_\+control -\/ apply control mask updates to the subtree @cgrp:\+ root of the target subtree

subsystems can be enabled and disabled in a subtree using the following steps.


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item Call \doxylink{cgroup_8c_aad3561142cafdf3275cb1b45d66d76e2}{cgroup\+\_\+save\+\_\+control()} to stash the current state.

\item Call \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a19691d198ec77937b2f7d1514e9b008a}{cgroup\+\_\+apply\+\_\+control()} to apply the changes.
\item Optionally perform other related operations.
\item Call \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a1305f3486e4bc06d2e5d636e9d6a77fe}{cgroup\+\_\+finalize\+\_\+control()} to finish up.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

This function implements step 3 and propagates the mask changes throughout @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s subtree, updates csses accordingly and perform process migrations.

cgroup\+\_\+apply\+\_\+control\+\_\+enable -\/ enable or show csses according to control @cgrp:\+ root of the target subtree

Walk @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s subtree and create new csses or make the existing ones visible. A css is created invisible if it\textquotesingle{}s being implicitly enabled through dependency. An invisible css is made visible when the userland explicitly enables it.

Returns 0 on success, -\/errno on failure. On failure, csses which have been processed already aren\textquotesingle{}t cleaned up. The caller is responsible for cleaning up with \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a92f0f057e48c2427acbab8995b6d20f0}{cgroup\+\_\+apply\+\_\+control\+\_\+disable()}.

Function Description:\+ Enables or shows csses according to control masks. It creates new csses and populates directories for enabled subsystems. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

void cgroup\+\_\+attach\+\_\+lock (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{enum \doxymbox{\hyperlink{cgroup-defs_8h_a6f88470278a2f9e2137cf0f8b6672f4a}{cgroup\+\_\+attach\+\_\+lock\+\_\+mode}}}]{lock\+\_\+mode}{, }\item[{struct task\+\_\+struct \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{tsk}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

cgroup\+\_\+attach\+\_\+lock -\/ Lock for -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}attach() @lock\+\_\+mode:\+ whether acquire and acquire which rwsem @tsk:\+ thread group to lock

cgroup migration sometimes needs to stabilize threadgroups against forks and exits by write-\/locking cgroup\+\_\+threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem. However, some -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}attach() implementations (e.\+g. cpuset), also need to disable CPU hotplug. Unfortunately, letting -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}attach() operations acquire cpus\+\_\+read\+\_\+lock() can lead to deadlocks.

Bringing up a CPU may involve creating and destroying tasks which requires read-\/locking threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem, so threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem nests inside cpus\+\_\+read\+\_\+lock(). If we call an -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}attach() which acquires the cpus lock while write-\/locking threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem, the locking order is reversed and we end up waiting for an on-\/going CPU hotplug operation which in turn is waiting for the threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem to be released to create new tasks. For more details:\+

\href{http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20220711174629.uehfmqegcwn2lqzu@wubuntu}{\texttt{http:\+/\+/\+lkml.\+kernel.\+org/\+r/\+20220711174629.\+uehfmqegcwn2lqzu@wubuntu}}

Resolve the situation by always acquiring cpus\+\_\+read\+\_\+lock() before optionally write-\/locking cgroup\+\_\+threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem. This allows -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}attach() to assume that CPU hotplug is disabled on entry.

When favordynmods is enabled, take per threadgroup rwsem to reduce overhead on dynamic cgroup modifications. see the comment above CGRP\+\_\+\+ROOT\+\_\+\+FAVOR\+\_\+\+DYNMODS definition.

tsk is not NULL only when writing to cgroup.\+procs.

Function Description:\+ Acquires locks for cgroup attach operations. It takes cpus\+\_\+read\+\_\+lock() and optionally write-\/locks cgroup\+\_\+threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem or per-\/threadgroup rwsem. This prevents CPU hotplug and threadgroup changes during migration.

cgroup\+\_\+css -\/ obtain a cgroup\textquotesingle{}s css for the specified subsystem @cgrp:\+ the cgroup of interest @ss:\+ the subsystem of interest (NULL returns @cgrp-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}self)

Return @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s css (\doxylink{structcgroup__subsys__state}{cgroup\+\_\+subsys\+\_\+state}) associated with @ss. This function must be called either under cgroup\+\_\+mutex or rcu\+\_\+read\+\_\+lock() and the caller is responsible for pinning the returned css if it wants to keep accessing it outside the said locks. This function may return NULL if @cgrp doesn\textquotesingle{}t have @subsys\+\_\+id enabled.

Function Description:\+ Returns a cgroup\textquotesingle{}s css (\doxylink{structcgroup__subsys__state}{cgroup\+\_\+subsys\+\_\+state}) for the specified subsystem. Must be called under cgroup\+\_\+mutex or RCU read lock. Returns NULL if the subsystem is not enabled for the cgroup.

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{cgroup_8c_a7292ee1bb2523ce7a2a95e3a99918ad9} 
int cgroup\+\_\+css\+\_\+set\+\_\+fork (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct kernel\+\_\+clone\+\_\+args \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{kargs}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption}) \&\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

cgroup\+\_\+css\+\_\+set\+\_\+fork -\/ find or create a \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} for a child process @kargs:\+ the arguments passed to create the child process

This functions finds or creates a new \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} which the child process will be attached to in \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ace93e156c02ebfd2bb8481618606b70f}{cgroup\+\_\+post\+\_\+fork()}. By default, the child process will be given the same \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} as its parent.

If CLONE\+\_\+\+INTO\+\_\+\+CGROUP is specified this function will try to find an existing \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} which includes the requested cgroup and if not create a new \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} that the child will be attached to later. If this function succeeds it will hold cgroup\+\_\+threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem on return. If CLONE\+\_\+\+INTO\+\_\+\+CGROUP is requested this function will grab cgroup mutex before grabbing cgroup\+\_\+threadgroup\+\_\+rwsem and will hold a reference to the target cgroup.

Function Description:\+ Finds or creates a \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} for a child process. It handles CLONE\+\_\+\+INTO\+\_\+\+CGROUP by finding the \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set} for the target cgroup. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

cgroup\+\_\+destroy\+\_\+locked -\/ destroy @cgrp (called on rmdir) @cgrp:\+ cgroup to be destroyed

Tear down @cgrp on behalf of rmdir. Constraints:\+


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Userspace:\+ rmdir must succeed when cgroup.\+procs and friends are empty.
\item Kernel:\+ subsystem -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() must not run while any task in @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s subtree is still doing kernel work. A task hidden from cgroup.\+procs (past exit\+\_\+signals() with signal-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}live cleared) can still schedule, allocate, and consume resources until its final context switch. Dying descendants in the subtree can host such tasks too.
\item Kernel:\+ \doxylink{cgroup__refcnt_8h_a3b2f377eebd0519d8f7d74f87723776d}{css\+\_\+tryget\+\_\+online()} must fail by the time -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() runs.
\end{DoxyItemize}

The destruction runs in three parts:\+


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item This function:\+ synchronous user-\/visible state teardown plus \doxylink{cgroup_8c_aebd4cc4de619e38b723a687cbc6daff4}{kill\+\_\+css\+\_\+sync()} on each subsystem css.
\item \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ad1989da629d77448961f7a254bc589f1}{cgroup\+\_\+finish\+\_\+destroy()}:\+ kicks the percpu\+\_\+ref kill via \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ad91a4a43d39654f252ada5e60ccb315a}{kill\+\_\+css\+\_\+finish()} on each subsystem css. Fires once @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s subtree is fully drained, either inline here or from \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ac908c84e503c31d93d2c7fbced3e985d}{cgroup\+\_\+update\+\_\+populated()}.
\item The percpu\+\_\+ref kill chain:\+ css\+\_\+killed\+\_\+ref\+\_\+fn -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} css\+\_\+killed\+\_\+work\+\_\+fn -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} release/\+free.
\end{DoxyItemize}

Return 0 on success, -\/EBUSY if a userspace-\/visible task or an online child remains.

cgroup\+\_\+e\+\_\+css -\/ obtain a cgroup\textquotesingle{}s effective css for the specified subsystem @cgrp:\+ the cgroup of interest @ss:\+ the subsystem of interest

Find and get the effective css of @cgrp for @ss. The effective css is defined as the matching css of the nearest ancestor including self which has @ss enabled. If @ss is not mounted on the hierarchy @cgrp is on, the root css is returned, so this function always returns a valid css.

The returned css is not guaranteed to be online, and therefore it is the callers responsibility to try get a reference for it.

Function Description:\+ Returns the effective css for a cgroup and subsystem, always returning a valid css. If the subsystem is not enabled on the cgroup\textquotesingle{}s hierarchy, it returns the root css. The returned css is not guaranteed to be online.

cgroup\+\_\+get\+\_\+e\+\_\+css -\/ get a cgroup\textquotesingle{}s effective css for the specified subsystem @cgrp:\+ the cgroup of interest @ss:\+ the subsystem of interest

Find and get the effective css of @cgrp for @ss. The effective css is defined as the matching css of the nearest ancestor including self which has @ss enabled. If @ss is not mounted on the hierarchy @cgrp is on, the root css is returned, so this function always returns a valid css. The returned css must be put using \doxylink{cgroup__refcnt_8h_a06a91a2613e85e6b114f4fc2ddd5dbc1}{css\+\_\+put()}.

Function Description:\+ Gets a reference to the effective css for a cgroup and subsystem. It finds the nearest ancestor with the subsystem enabled and tries to get an online reference. Returns the css with a reference taken, or NULL.

struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup}{cgroup}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} cgroup\+\_\+kn\+\_\+lock\+\_\+live (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct kernfs\+\_\+node \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{kn}{, }\item[{bool}]{drain\+\_\+offline}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

cgroup\+\_\+kn\+\_\+lock\+\_\+live -\/ locking helper for cgroup kernfs methods @kn:\+ the kernfs\+\_\+node being serviced @drain\+\_\+offline:\+ perform offline draining on the cgroup

This helper is to be used by a cgroup kernfs method currently servicing @kn. It breaks the active protection, performs cgroup locking and verifies that the associated cgroup is alive. Returns the cgroup if alive; otherwise, NULL. A successful return should be undone by a matching \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a5808e21adbb735b336c1ac679347c4f4}{cgroup\+\_\+kn\+\_\+unlock()} invocation. If @drain\+\_\+offline is true, the cgroup is drained of offlining csses before return.

Any cgroup kernfs method implementation which requires locking the associated cgroup should use this helper. It avoids nesting cgroup locking under kernfs active protection and allows all kernfs operations including self-\/removal.

Function Description:\+ Locks a cgroup\textquotesingle{}s kernfs node and returns the cgroup if it\textquotesingle{}s live (online). It breaks active protection, acquires cgroup\+\_\+mutex, and verifies the cgroup is not dead. Returns the cgroup or NULL.

cgroup\+\_\+lock\+\_\+and\+\_\+drain\+\_\+offline -\/ lock cgroup\+\_\+mutex and drain offlined csses @cgrp:\+ root of the target subtree

Because css offlining is asynchronous, userland may try to re-\/enable a controller while the previous css is still around. This function grabs cgroup\+\_\+mutex and drains the previous css instances of @cgrp\textquotesingle{}s subtree.

Function Description:\+ Locks cgroup\+\_\+mutex and drains offline csses. It waits for any dying csses to complete before returning. Used when making changes that require stable css states.

cgroup\+\_\+migrate -\/ migrate a process or task to a cgroup @leader:\+ the leader of the process or the task to migrate @threadgroup:\+ whether @leader points to the whole process or a single task @mgctx:\+ migration context

The caller is also responsible for invoking \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ae1c005f2422d148d0359a2032fb9e291}{cgroup\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+add\+\_\+src()} and \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a10644a3466731282fcec4423bbad0343}{cgroup\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+prepare\+\_\+dst()} on the targets before invoking this function and following up with \doxylink{cgroup_8c_aa7e924fc6912f50590ab05ee0f7bb029}{cgroup\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+finish()}.

As long as a controller\textquotesingle{}s -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}can\+\_\+attach() doesn\textquotesingle{}t fail, this function is guaranteed to succeed. This means that, excluding -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}can\+\_\+attach() failure, when migrating multiple targets, the success or failure can be decided for all targets by invoking group\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+prepare\+\_\+dst() before actually starting migrating.

cgroup\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+prepare\+\_\+dst -\/ prepare destination css\+\_\+sets for migration @mgctx:\+ migration context

Tasks are about to be moved and all the source css\+\_\+sets have been preloaded to @mgctx-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}preloaded\+\_\+src\+\_\+csets. This function looks up and pins all destination css\+\_\+sets, links each to its source, and append them to @mgctx-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}preloaded\+\_\+dst\+\_\+csets.

This function must be called after \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ae1c005f2422d148d0359a2032fb9e291}{cgroup\+\_\+migrate\+\_\+add\+\_\+src()} has been called on each migration source \doxylink{structcss__set}{css\+\_\+set}. {\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{cgroup_8c_aa8e9c07d7c652eb98e9053203c68b444} 
bool cgroup\+\_\+on\+\_\+dfl (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup}{cgroup}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{cgrp}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

cgroup\+\_\+on\+\_\+dfl -\/ test whether a cgroup is on the default hierarchy @cgrp:\+ the cgroup of interest

The default hierarchy is the v2 interface of cgroup and this function can be used to test whether a cgroup is on the default hierarchy for cases where a subsystem should behave differently depending on the interface version.

List of changed behaviors:\+


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Mount options "{}noprefix"{}, "{}xattr"{}, "{}clone\+\_\+children"{}, "{}release\+\_\+agent"{} and "{}name"{} are disallowed.
\item When mounting an existing superblock, mount options should match.
\item rename(2) is disallowed.
\item "{}tasks"{} is removed. Everything should be at process granularity. Use "{}cgroup.\+procs"{} instead.
\item "{}cgroup.\+procs"{} is not sorted. pids will be unique unless they got recycled in-\/between reads.
\item "{}release\+\_\+agent"{} and "{}notify\+\_\+on\+\_\+release"{} are removed. Replacement notification mechanism will be implemented.
\item "{}cgroup.\+clone\+\_\+children"{} is removed.
\item "{}cgroup.\+subtree\+\_\+populated"{} is available. Its value is 0 if the cgroup and its descendants contain no task; otherwise, 1. The file also generates kernfs notification which can be monitored through poll and \+[di]\+notify when the value of the file changes.
\item cpuset:\+ tasks will be kept in empty cpusets when hotplug happens and take masks of ancestors with non-\/empty cpus/\+mems, instead of being moved to an ancestor.
\item cpuset:\+ a task can be moved into an empty cpuset, and again it takes masks of ancestors.
\item blkcg:\+ blk-\/throttle becomes properly hierarchical.
\end{DoxyItemize}

Function Description:\+ Tests whether a cgroup is on the default (v2) hierarchy. Returns true if the cgroup\textquotesingle{}s root is the default root. This is used to determine which behavior and features apply to the cgroup.

cgroup\+\_\+update\+\_\+dfl\+\_\+csses -\/ update css assoc of a subtree in default hierarchy @cgrp:\+ root of the subtree to update csses for

@cgrp\textquotesingle{}s control masks have changed and its subtree\textquotesingle{}s css associations need to be updated accordingly. This function looks up all css\+\_\+sets which are attached to the subtree, creates the matching updated css\+\_\+sets and migrates the tasks to the new ones.

Function Description:\+ Updates css associations in a subtree on the default hierarchy. It migrates tasks to new css\+\_\+sets when control masks change. Returns 0 on success or a negative error code.

void cgroup\+\_\+update\+\_\+populated (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup}{cgroup}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{cgrp}{, }\item[{bool}]{populated}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

cgroup\+\_\+update\+\_\+populated -\/ update the populated count of a cgroup @cgrp:\+ the target cgroup @populated:\+ inc or dec populated count

One of the css\+\_\+sets associated with @cgrp is either getting its first task or losing the last. Update @cgrp-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}nr\+\_\+populated\+\_\+\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} accordingly. The count is propagated towards root so that a given cgroup\textquotesingle{}s nr\+\_\+populated\+\_\+children is zero iff none of its descendants contain any tasks.

@cgrp\textquotesingle{}s interface file "{}cgroup.\+populated"{} is zero if both @cgrp-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}nr\+\_\+populated\+\_\+csets and @cgrp-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}nr\+\_\+populated\+\_\+children are zero and 1 otherwise. When the sum changes from or to zero, userland is notified that the content of the interface file has changed. This can be used to detect when @cgrp and its descendants become populated or empty.

Function Description:\+ Updates the populated counters of a cgroup and its ancestors. It increments or decrements the populated cset count and propagates the change up the hierarchy. When the populated state changes, it notifies userland via the cgroup.\+events file.

css destruction is four-\/stage process.


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item Destruction starts. Killing of the percpu\+\_\+ref is initiated. Implemented in \doxylink{cgroup_8c_ad91a4a43d39654f252ada5e60ccb315a}{kill\+\_\+css\+\_\+finish()}.
\item When the percpu\+\_\+ref is confirmed to be visible as killed on all CPUs and thus \doxylink{cgroup__refcnt_8h_a3b2f377eebd0519d8f7d74f87723776d}{css\+\_\+tryget\+\_\+online()} is guaranteed to fail, the css can be offlined by invoking \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a8f4e28a37a77a7d80deccea743e1c543}{offline\+\_\+css()}. After offlining, the base ref is put. Implemented in \doxylink{cgroup_8c_acc42610cb0f36143ec468f8ccf5be3a7}{css\+\_\+killed\+\_\+work\+\_\+fn()}.
\item When the percpu\+\_\+ref reaches zero, the only possible remaining accessors are inside RCU read sections. \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a6a4e0c39b21139adda760918afcd420c}{css\+\_\+release()} schedules the RCU callback.
\item After the grace period, the css can be freed. Implemented in \doxylink{cgroup_8c_a76cd83d0444fe6888871c4e2d341791d}{css\+\_\+free\+\_\+rwork\+\_\+fn()}.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

It is actually hairier because both step 2 and 4 require process context and thus involve punting to css-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}destroy\+\_\+work adding two additional steps to the already complex sequence.

Function Description:\+ RCU work function for freeing a css. It frees the css and its associated resources. Called after the RCU grace period.

css\+\_\+next\+\_\+child -\/ find the next child of a given css @pos:\+ the current position (NULL to initiate traversal) @parent:\+ css whose children to walk

This function returns the next child of @parent and should be called under either cgroup\+\_\+mutex or RCU read lock. The only requirement is that @parent and @pos are accessible. The next sibling is guaranteed to be returned regardless of their states.

If a subsystem synchronizes -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() and the start of iteration, a css which finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() is guaranteed to be visible in the future iterations and will stay visible until the last reference is put. A css which hasn\textquotesingle{}t finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() or already finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() may show up during traversal. It\textquotesingle{}s each subsystem\textquotesingle{}s responsibility to synchronize against on/\+offlining.

Function Description:\+ Returns the next child css of a parent. This is the RCU-\/safe version of walking css children. Used for iteration over css children.

css\+\_\+next\+\_\+descendant\+\_\+post -\/ find the next descendant for post-\/order walk @pos:\+ the current position (NULL to initiate traversal) @root:\+ css whose descendants to walk

To be used by css\+\_\+for\+\_\+each\+\_\+descendant\+\_\+post(). Find the next descendant to visit for post-\/order traversal of @root\textquotesingle{}s descendants. @root is included in the iteration and the last node to be visited.

While this function requires cgroup\+\_\+mutex or RCU read locking, it doesn\textquotesingle{}t require the whole traversal to be contained in a single critical section. Additionally, it isn\textquotesingle{}t necessary to hold onto a reference to @pos. This function will return the correct next descendant as long as both @pos and @cgroup are accessible and @pos is a descendant of @cgroup.

If a subsystem synchronizes -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() and the start of iteration, a css which finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() is guaranteed to be visible in the future iterations and will stay visible until the last reference is put. A css which hasn\textquotesingle{}t finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() or already finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() may show up during traversal. It\textquotesingle{}s each subsystem\textquotesingle{}s responsibility to synchronize against on/\+offlining.

struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup__subsys__state}{cgroup\+\_\+subsys\+\_\+state}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} css\+\_\+next\+\_\+descendant\+\_\+pre (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup__subsys__state}{cgroup\+\_\+subsys\+\_\+state}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{pos}{, }\item[{struct \doxymbox{\hyperlink{structcgroup__subsys__state}{cgroup\+\_\+subsys\+\_\+state}} \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{root}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

css\+\_\+next\+\_\+descendant\+\_\+pre -\/ find the next descendant for pre-\/order walk @pos:\+ the current position (NULL to initiate traversal) @root:\+ css whose descendants to walk

To be used by css\+\_\+for\+\_\+each\+\_\+descendant\+\_\+pre(). Find the next descendant to visit for pre-\/order traversal of @root\textquotesingle{}s descendants. @root is included in the iteration and the first node to be visited.

While this function requires cgroup\+\_\+mutex or RCU read locking, it doesn\textquotesingle{}t require the whole traversal to be contained in a single critical section. Additionally, it isn\textquotesingle{}t necessary to hold onto a reference to @pos. This function will return the correct next descendant as long as both @pos and @root are accessible and @pos is a descendant of @root.

If a subsystem synchronizes -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() and the start of iteration, a css which finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() is guaranteed to be visible in the future iterations and will stay visible until the last reference is put. A css which hasn\textquotesingle{}t finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+online() or already finished -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}css\+\_\+offline() may show up during traversal. It\textquotesingle{}s each subsystem\textquotesingle{}s responsibility to synchronize against on/\+offlining.

Function Description:\+ Returns the next descendant for pre-\/order traversal. It visits the root first, then children recursively. Used for pre-\/order iteration over css descendants.

css\+\_\+rightmost\+\_\+descendant -\/ return the rightmost descendant of a css @pos:\+ css of interest

Return the rightmost descendant of @pos. If there\textquotesingle{}s no descendant, @pos is returned. This can be used during pre-\/order traversal to skip subtree of @pos.

While this function requires cgroup\+\_\+mutex or RCU read locking, it doesn\textquotesingle{}t require the whole traversal to be contained in a single critical section. Additionally, it isn\textquotesingle{}t necessary to hold onto a reference to @pos. This function will return the correct rightmost descendant as long as @pos is accessible.

Function Description:\+ Returns the rightmost descendant of a css. It walks down the children list to find the last descendant. Used for post-\/order traversal optimization.

\doxylink{cgroup_8c_a4f216031bbabb938f020febda802d3c6}{cgroup\+\_\+task\+\_\+dead()} is called from finish\+\_\+task\+\_\+switch() which doesn\textquotesingle{}t allow scheduling even in RT. As the task\+\_\+dead path requires grabbing css\+\_\+set\+\_\+lock, this lead to sleeping in the invalid context warning bug. css\+\_\+set\+\_\+lock is too big to become a raw\+\_\+spinlock. The task\+\_\+dead path doesn\textquotesingle{}t need to run synchronously but can\textquotesingle{}t be delayed indefinitely either as the dead task pins the cgroup and task\+\_\+struct can be pinned indefinitely. Bounce through lazy irq\+\_\+work to allow batching while ensuring timely completion. \Hypertarget{cgroup_8c_a341f54ef56bd7593066085d76113cbca}\index{cgroup.c@{cgroup.c}!DEFINE\_PERCPU\_RWSEM@{DEFINE\_PERCPU\_RWSEM}}

Variable Description:\+ This structure defines the filesystem context operations for cgroup1 (legacy hierarchy) mounts. It contains function pointers for freeing the context (cgroup\+\_\+fs\+\_\+context\+\_\+free), parsing mount parameters (cgroup1\+\_\+parse\+\_\+param), getting the filesystem tree (cgroup1\+\_\+get\+\_\+tree), and reconfiguring the mount (cgroup1\+\_\+reconfigure). These operations handle the older cgroup1 mount behavior with subsystem selection, named hierarchies, and release agent support.

Variable Description:\+ This is an array of filesystem parameter specifications for cgroup2 mount options. Each entry defines a valid mount flag and its corresponding enum value from \doxylink{cgroup_8c_af4ef2481171a0a19ee0f4d5e12ea3616}{cgroup2\+\_\+param}. cgroup core interface files for the default hierarchy

Variable Description:\+ This is an array of cftype structures defining the core interface files for the cgroup v2 (default) hierarchy. Each entry represents a file that appears in cgroup directories, with handlers for reading and writing. The files include cgroup.\+type (control threaded mode), cgroup.\+procs (list and move processes), cgroup.\+threads (list and move threads), cgroup.\+controllers (show available controllers), \doxylink{structcgroup_abf73958a93559264534c5c7f8b4c8ef8}{cgroup.\+subtree\+\_\+control} (enable/\+disable controllers for children), cgroup.\+events (populated and frozen status), cgroup.\+max.\+descendants (limit descendant count), cgroup.\+max.\+depth (limit hierarchy depth), cgroup.\+stat (statistics), cgroup.\+stat.\+local (local statistics), cgroup.\+freeze (freeze/\+unfreeze cgroup), cgroup.\+kill (kill all processes in cgroup), cpu.\+stat (CPU statistics), and cpu.\+stat.\+local (local CPU statistics). The array is terminated by an empty entry.

A task must hold cgroup\+\_\+mutex to modify cgroups.

Any task can increment and decrement the count field without lock. So in general, code holding cgroup\+\_\+mutex can\textquotesingle{}t rely on the count field not changing. However, if the count goes to zero, then only \doxylink{cgroup_8c_acdcee710167815f30e8a48d607e160fb}{cgroup\+\_\+attach\+\_\+task()} can increment it again. Because a count of zero means that no tasks are currently attached, therefore there is no way a task attached to that cgroup can fork (the other way to increment the count). So code holding cgroup\+\_\+mutex can safely assume that if the count is zero, it will stay zero. Similarly, if a task holds cgroup\+\_\+mutex on a cgroup with zero count, it knows that the cgroup won\textquotesingle{}t be removed, as \doxylink{cgroup_8c_abed96bdb67eb267dff3c4e0535215a3c}{cgroup\+\_\+rmdir()} needs that mutex.

A cgroup can only be deleted if both its \textquotesingle{}count\textquotesingle{} of using tasks is zero, and its list of \textquotesingle{}children\textquotesingle{} cgroups is empty. Since all tasks in the system use {\itshape some} cgroup, and since there is always at least one task in the system (init, pid == 1), therefore, root cgroup always has either children cgroups and/\+or using tasks. So we don\textquotesingle{}t need a special hack to ensure that root cgroup cannot be deleted.

P.\+S. One more locking exception. RCU is used to guard the update of a tasks cgroup pointer by \doxylink{cgroup_8c_acdcee710167815f30e8a48d607e160fb}{cgroup\+\_\+attach\+\_\+task()}

Variable Description:\+ This structure defines the kernfs syscall operations for the cgroup v2 (default) hierarchy. It contains function pointers for showing mount options (cgroup\+\_\+show\+\_\+options), creating directories (cgroup\+\_\+mkdir), removing directories (cgroup\+\_\+rmdir), and showing the filesystem path (cgroup\+\_\+show\+\_\+path). These operations are used by the VFS layer when interacting with cgroup2 filesystem directories, handling operations like directory creation (mkdir), deletion (rmdir), and path resolution.

\Hypertarget{cgroup_8c_a5435e58a83f25565c685012519c4f7dc}\index{cgroup.c@{cgroup.c}!cgroup\_offline\_wq@{cgroup\_offline\_wq}}
\index{cgroup\_offline\_wq@{cgroup\_offline\_wq}!cgroup.c@{cgroup.c}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{cgroup\_offline\_wq}{cgroup\_offline\_wq}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{cgroup_8c_a5435e58a83f25565c685012519c4f7dc} 
struct workqueue\+\_\+struct\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} cgroup\+\_\+offline\+\_\+wq\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [static]}}

cgroup destruction makes heavy use of work items and there can be a lot of concurrent destructions. Use a separate workqueue so that cgroup destruction work items don\textquotesingle{}t end up filling up max\+\_\+active of system\+\_\+percpu\+\_\+wq which may lead to deadlock.

A cgroup destruction should enqueue work sequentially to:\+ cgroup\+\_\+offline\+\_\+wq:\+ use for css offline work cgroup\+\_\+release\+\_\+wq:\+ use for css release work cgroup\+\_\+free\+\_\+wq:\+ use for free work

Rationale for using separate workqueues:\+ The cgroup root free work may depend on completion of other css offline operations. If all tasks were enqueued to a single workqueue, this could create a deadlock scenario where:\+
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item Free work waits for other css offline work to complete.
\item But other css offline work is queued after free work in the same queue.
\end{DoxyItemize}

Example deadlock scenario with single workqueue (cgroup\+\_\+destroy\+\_\+wq):\+
\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item umount net\+\_\+prio
\item net\+\_\+prio root destruction enqueues work to cgroup\+\_\+destroy\+\_\+wq (CPUx)
\item perf\+\_\+event CSS A offline enqueues work to same cgroup\+\_\+destroy\+\_\+wq (CPUx)
\item net\+\_\+prio cgroup\+\_\+destroy\+\_\+root-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}cgroup\+\_\+lock\+\_\+and\+\_\+drain\+\_\+offline.
\item net\+\_\+prio root destruction blocks waiting for perf\+\_\+event CSS A offline, which can never complete as it\textquotesingle{}s behind in the same queue and workqueue\textquotesingle{}s max\+\_\+active is 1. 
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

Variable Description:\+ This is an array of cftype structures defining the PSI (Pressure Stall Information) files for cgroups. These files are conditionally present when CONFIG\+\_\+\+PSI is enabled. The files include io.\+pressure (I/\+O pressure), memory.\+pressure (memory pressure), cpu.\+pressure (CPU pressure), irq.\+pressure (IRQ pressure, when CONFIG\+\_\+\+IRQ\+\_\+\+TIME\+\_\+\+ACCOUNTING is enabled), and cgroup.\+pressure (control PSI enable/\+disable). Each pressure file supports reading pressure statistics, writing to create triggers, polling for events, and release cleanup. The cgroup.\+pressure file controls whether PSI is enabled for the cgroup. The array is terminated by an empty entry.

the default hierarchy

Variable Description:\+ This is the default (v2) cgroup hierarchy root. It is always present and serves as the main hierarchy for cgroup v2 operations. It contains the root cgroup with preallocated per-\/\+CPU rstat (recursive statistics) data structures for CPU and base statistics. This root is created during boot and is used when the cgroup2 filesystem is mounted.

Assign a monotonically increasing serial number to csses. It guarantees cgroups with bigger numbers are newer than those with smaller numbers. Also, as csses are always appended to the parent\textquotesingle{}s -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}children list, it guarantees that sibling csses are always sorted in the ascending serial number order on the list. Protected by cgroup\+\_\+mutex.
